figures.finding: A payer in Kiribati must withhold tax at the standard 30% from dividends, interest, royalties, natural resource payments and management charges paid to a non-resident, and pay it within 15 days after the month's end; payments to non-residents for services are also subject to withholding at the applicable rate.
figures.applies: The rate on a non-resident's fee for services (a performer's) was not stated.

sources.said: The payer shall withhold the tax levied on dividend, interest, royalty, natural resource payment and management charge that paid to a non-resident at the standard tax rate of 30%.
Every employer, principal or payer, as the case may be, shall pay to the Board the amount of any tax withheld within 15 days after the end of the month in which the tax was so withheld.

any person or entity making payments to non-residents for services, interest, royalties, or other income sourced in Kiribati is legally required to withhold tax at the applicable rate and remit it to the Kiribati Tax Office.

figures.finding: Every employer or payer remits tax withheld within 15 days after the end of the month and lodges an annual statement within 21 days after the tax year.

sources.said: Every employer, principal or payer, as the case may be, shall pay to the Board the amount of any tax withheld within 15 days after the end of the month in which the tax was so withheld.
Every payer who is required to withhold tax shall, within 21 days after the end of each tax year

figures.finding: An employee pays 7.5% of his total earnings to the Kiribati Provident Fund and the employer matches it (15% in all), remitted monthly by the employer; no ceiling is stated.

sources.said: Contributions should be calculated in respect of total earnings of the employee such as Salary/Wage for instance in a fortnight pay calculation is as follows. • employee share from Basic Salary/Wage of $120 * 7.5% is equal to $9.00 • employer share for the deduction made is $9.00 • both shares as a compulsory rate of 15% is equivalent to $18.00

sources.title: The payer's tax obligation on international payments (sections 90, 117 and 121 of the Income Tax Act), fact sheet (Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, Kiribati)
sources.said: The payer shall withhold the tax levied on dividend, interest, royalty, natural resource payment and management charge that paid to a non-resident at the standard tax rate of 30%. … Every employer, principal or payer, as the case may be, shall pay to the Board the amount of any tax withheld within 15 days after the end of the month in which the tax was so withheld. … Every payer who is required to withhold tax shall, within 21 days after the end of each tax year

sources.title: The Payer’s Tax Obligation on International Payments (Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, Kiribati)
sources.said: any person or entity making payments to non-residents for services, interest, royalties, or other income sourced in Kiribati is legally required to withhold tax at the applicable rate and remit it to the Kiribati Tax Office.

sources.title: Kiribati Provident Fund, FAQ: How is my Provident Fund contribution calculated?
sources.said: Contributions should be calculated in respect of total earnings of the employee such as Salary/Wage for instance in a fortnight pay calculation is as follows. • employee share from Basic Salary/Wage of $120 * 7.5% is equal to $9.00 • employer share for the deduction made is $9.00 • both shares as a compulsory rate of 15% is equivalent to $18.00
